newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan lending surges again, up 6 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan lending surges again, up 6 pct in July.

text.p: Venezuelan commercial bank loans surged six percent in July to 3.5 trillion bolivars ($7 billion), continuing the past year's rises, Softline consultants reported.

According to the firm's monthly roundup of 40 commercial banks, Venezuelan bank credit portfolios are now up 148 percent over the past 12 months, compared with inflation over the same period of 40.5 percent.

Bank deposits meanwhile rose 6.5 percent to 6.5 trillion bolivars in July, the firm reported, with Banco Provincial still the largest accounts holder by a large margin at nearly 1.5 trillion bolivars.
Banco Mercantil meanwhile accounts for 912 billion bolivars of deposits, and Banco de Venezuela 582 billion.

The near parallel increases in new deposits and loans left the banking sector's intermediation index largely flat at 50.4 percent. The index describes the amount banks lend per each bolivar deposited.
As a percentage of bank assets, loans now account for 41.8 percent, while investments in securities, at 2.4 trillion bolivars, account for 28.3 percent, Softline said.
Softline added that bank capitalization rates, or the ratio of shareholders' equity to total assets, was 12.8 percent in July.
